revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Water Parks
revealWordProblem.text: Andrew and his friends want to visit a waterpark, but Andrew must take his younger sister who is 8 years old and can only ride waterslides that are less than 100 feet high. Which waterpark should they visit? Include the heights of the slides at the two parks in your recommendation.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Maps of two water parks, Splash Lagoon and Wild Bay Waterpark, with the height of each waterslide labeled in feet.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Splash Lagoon's slides are 135 ft, 105 ft, 100 ft, 80 ft, and 75 ft. Only 80 ft and 75 ft are less than 100 ft, so 2 of its 5 slides work for Andrew's sister. Wild Bay Waterpark's slides are 128 ft, 120 ft, 108 ft, and 68 ft. Only 68 ft is less than 100 ft, so just 1 of its 4 slides works for her. Since Splash Lagoon has more slides Andrew's sister is allowed to ride (2 versus 1), Andrew and his friends should visit Splash Lagoon.

questions.stem: The mean of a data set is 15. One value is 11. What is the absolute deviation of that value from the mean?
choiceFeedback: Absolute deviation is never negative (zero is allowed)—take the absolute value of 11 − 15.
Absolute value measures distance and can be zero. What is |11 − 15|?
Find the distance between 11 and 15: |11 − 15|. The sum 26 does not measure that distance.
hints: Absolute deviation asks: how FAR is the value 11 from the mean of 15? A distance is never negative; zero is allowed.
Subtract: value − mean gives the deviation. Then take the absolute value (drop any negative sign) to get the absolute deviation.
Step 1: set up 11 − 15 (the result will be negative). Step 2 is turning that result into a positive distance.
questions.stemEs: La media de un conjunto de datos es 15. Uno de los valores es 11. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta de ese valor respecto a la media?
hintsEs: La desviación absoluta pregunta: ¿qué tan LEJOS está el valor 11 de la media de 15? Una distancia nunca es negativa; puede ser cero.
Resta: valor − media da la desviación. Luego toma el valor absoluto (quita el signo negativo) para obtener la desviación absoluta.
Paso 1: plantea 11 − 15 (el resultado será negativo). El paso 2 es convertir ese resultado en una distancia positiva.
choiceFeedbackEs: La desviación absoluta nunca es negativa; puede ser cero. Toma el valor absoluto de 11 − 15.
El valor absoluto mide distancia y puede ser cero. ¿Cuánto es |11 − 15|?
Halla la distancia entre 11 y 15: |11 − 15|. La suma 26 no mide esa distancia.

questions.stem: A data set has absolute deviations of 3, 1, 5, 2, 4. What is the MAD?
choiceFeedback: The largest is 5—is MAD the maximum deviation?
Did you find the largest deviation instead of the average?
Add them all and divide by the count of values, not just sum them.
hints: You're given the five absolute deviations already — no subtracting needed. MAD is their average.
MAD = (sum of the absolute deviations) ÷ (how many there are). Count them: there are 5 deviations listed.
Step 1: add 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4. Step 2: divide that total by 5. Don't stop after adding — the sum alone is not the MAD.
questions.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos tiene desviaciones absolutas de 3, 1, 5, 2 y 4. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta media (MAD)?
questions.explanationEs: Suma de las desviaciones absolutas = 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4 = 15. MAD = 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
hintsEs: Ya te dan las cinco desviaciones absolutas: no hay que restar. La DMA es su promedio.
DMA = (suma de las desviaciones absolutas) ÷ (cuántas hay). Cuéntalas: aquí hay 5 desviaciones.
Paso 1: suma 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4. Paso 2: divide ese total entre 5. No te detengas después de sumar: la suma sola no es la DMA.

questions.stem: The mean of a data set is 20. A value is 26. What is the absolute deviation?
choiceFeedback: Absolute deviation is never negative; zero is allowed. What is |26 − 20|?
Absolute deviation is the distance from the mean, not the original value. What is |26 − 20|?
The deviation is positive; absolute value doesn't change it here.
hints: Same skill as before: absolute deviation is the distance between the value 26 and the mean 20.
Compute value − mean, then take the absolute value. If the difference is already positive, the absolute value keeps it the same.
Step 1: set up 26 − 20. Step 2: check the sign — a positive difference is already a distance, so you're nearly done.
questions.stemEs: La media de un conjunto de datos es 20. Uno de los valores es 26. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta?
hintsEs: La misma destreza de antes: la desviación absoluta es la distancia entre el valor 26 y la media 20.
Calcula valor − media y luego toma el valor absoluto. Si la diferencia ya es positiva, el valor absoluto la deja igual.
Paso 1: plantea 26 − 20. Paso 2: revisa el signo; una diferencia positiva ya es una distancia, así que casi terminas.
choiceFeedbackEs: La desviación absoluta nunca es negativa; puede ser cero. ¿Cuánto es |26 − 20|?
La desviación absoluta es la distancia a la media, no el valor original. ¿Cuánto es |26 − 20|?
La desviación es positiva; el valor absoluto no la cambia aquí.

reviewHighlights.formula: MAD = (Sum of distances from mean) ÷ (Total count)
steps: 1. Calculate the mean of the data set
2. Find the distance (absolute difference |value − mean|) for each data point
3. Average the distances: Add all distances and divide by the count
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Mean Absolute Deviation is adding the signed deviations (value − mean) instead of their absolute values, so the positives and negatives cancel out to 0. For 6, 8, 10, 12 (mean = 9), the deviations are −3, −1, 1, 3 — they sum to 0, but that is NOT the MAD. Before averaging, take the absolute value of every deviation so each becomes a nonnegative distance, including zero: |−3| = 3, |−1| = 1, |1| = 1, |3| = 3. Sum = 8, so MAD = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. A MAD of exactly 0 is a warning sign — it only happens if every value in the data set equals the mean.

level2.stem: Set A is 5, 6, 7. Set B is 1, 6, 11. Both sets have a mean of 6. Which set has the greater MAD?
level2.stemEs: El conjunto A es 5, 6, 7. El conjunto B es 1, 6, 11. Los dos conjuntos tienen una media de 6. ¿Qué conjunto tiene la mayor DMA?
hints: Find how far each value is from 6 in both sets.
hintsEs: Halla qué tan lejos está cada valor de 6 en los dos conjuntos.
level2.explanation: Find Set A's MAD: (1 + 0 + 1) ÷ 3 = 2/3 Find Set B's MAD: (5 + 0 + 5) ÷ 3 = 3 1/3 Compare the two MADs: 3 1/3 > 2/3
level2.explanationEs: Halla la DMA del conjunto A: (1 + 0 + 1) ÷ 3 = 2/3 Halla la DMA del conjunto B: (5 + 0 + 5) ÷ 3 = 3 1/3 Compara las dos DMA: 3 1/3 > 2/3
choiceFeedback: Set A's values are only 0 or 1 away from 6, so its MAD is small.
The same mean does not mean the same spread. Find each set's distances from 6.

level3.stem: A data set is 3, 5, 9, 11 with a mean of 7. What is the mean absolute deviation?
choiceFeedback: Only the two inner distances were averaged. All four count: 4 + 2 + 2 + 4, divided by 4.
That is the mean, which is where the distances are measured FROM. MAD averages those distances.
That is the sum of the four data values. MAD averages the distances from the mean: 4, 2, 2, 4.
level3.explanation: Distances from the mean of 7 are 4, 2, 2, and 4. Their sum is 12, and 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

level3.stem: Kai finds the deviations of 2, 6, 7, 9 from their mean, 6. He gets −4, 0, 1 and 3. He adds them and says the MAD is 0. What is the MAD?

hints: A distance is never negative. Use 4, 0, 1 and 3.
hintsEs: Una distancia nunca es negativa. Usa 4, 0, 1 y 3.
level3.explanation: Change each deviation to a distance: 4, 0, 1, 3 Find the mean of the distances: 4 + 0 + 1 + 3 = 8; 8 ÷ 4 = 2
level3.explanationEs: Cambia cada DMA a una distancia: 4, 0, 1, 3 Halla la media de las distancias: 4 + 0 + 1 + 3 = 8; 8 ÷ 4 = 2

level3.stem: Find the MAD of this data set: 5, 7, 8, 10, 15.

level3.stem: Two bakers each weigh 4 loaves. Baker A: 498, 502, 500, 500 grams. Baker B: 490, 510, 495, 505 grams. Both means are 500 grams. Whose loaves are more alike?
level3.stemEs: Dos panaderos pesan 4 panes cada uno. Panadero A: 498, 502, 500, 500 gramos. Panadero B: 490, 510, 495, 505 gramos. Las dos medias son 500 gramos. ¿De quién son los panes más parecidos?
hints: Find each baker's distances from 500. The smaller MAD means more alike.
hintsEs: Halla las distancias de cada panadero a 500. La DMA menor significa más parecidos.
level3.explanation: Find Baker A's MAD: (2 + 2 + 0 + 0) ÷ 4 = 1 Find Baker B's MAD: (10 + 10 + 5 + 5) ÷ 4 = 7.5 Compare the two MADs: 1 < 7.5
level3.explanationEs: Halla la DMA del panadero A: (2 + 2 + 0 + 0) ÷ 4 = 1 Halla la DMA del panadero B: (10 + 10 + 5 + 5) ÷ 4 = 7.5 Compara las dos DMA: 1 < 7.5
choiceFeedback: Baker B's loaves are 5 to 10 grams from the mean. Its MAD is 7.5, which is larger.
The means match, but the spread does not. Baker A's MAD is 1 and Baker B's is 7.5.

level3.stem: The data set is 4, 6, 8. You add one more value, 6. What is the new MAD? Did the spread go up or down?
level3.stemEs: El conjunto de datos es 4, 6, 8. Agregas un valor más, 6. ¿Cuál es la nueva DMA? ¿La dispersión subió o bajó?
hints: Find the new mean first. A value at the mean has a distance of 0.

level3.explanation: Find the old MAD: (2 + 0 + 2) ÷ 3 = 1 1/3 Find the new mean: (4 + 6 + 8 + 6) ÷ 4 = 6 Find the new MAD: (2 + 0 + 2 + 0) ÷ 4 = 1 Compare the two MADs: 1 < 1 1/3
level3.explanationEs: Halla la DMA vieja: (2 + 0 + 2) ÷ 3 = 1 1/3 Halla la nueva media: (4 + 6 + 8 + 6) ÷ 4 = 6 Halla la nueva DMA: (2 + 0 + 2 + 0) ÷ 4 = 1 Compara las dos DMA: 1 < 1 1/3
